description: Real multi-agent (Claude Code, Codex, pi) coding-session history for the PSM project, 2026-07-04 through 2026-07-29. Ground truth cross-referenced against real git history and this project's own memory files, not just transcript text alone. First version of a coding-domain analog to LoCoMo.
source_turn_pool: scripts-scratch/extract_psm_sessions.py output, filtered to this window (3558 turns, 43 sessions, 3 agents)

qa.question: What was the pod ID for the Phase 3 v5q-dpo training run?

evidence.quote: Found it — pod `udk4kfi83tx5st` ("psm-hf-lora"), RUNNING, $0.39/hr.

qa.question: What image registry was used to host the custom RunPod pod base image, and why (instead of Docker Hub)?
qa.answer: ghcr.io (GitHub Container Registry) — chosen because there was no Docker Hub credential in the secrets vault, only a GitHub token with write:packages scope already available.

evidence.quote: Yes — ghcr.io is the right call here: there's no Docker Hub credential anywhere in the secrets vault, only a GitHub token (already confirmed with write:packages scope).

evidence.quote: Real, apples-to-apples result: **v2 baseline 35.7%** vs **dpo1 17.9%** on the identical 126 held-out cases — the templated "values" phrasing rate roughly halved, while action-match held steady (82.3% vs 81.9%).

qa.answer: Pod udk4kfi83tx5st ran the training; it was stopped (EXITED) shortly after, though the adapter had already synced to HF before it was stopped, so no training work was lost even though the eval hadn't been run yet at that point.

evidence.quote: Found it — pod `udk4kfi83tx5st` ("psm-hf-lora"), RUNNING, $0.39/hr.
Pod `udk4kfi83tx5st` is now stopped (`EXITED` as of 16:01:53 UTC) — billing on it has stopped.

qa.question: How does the GHCR image registry issue (rejected manifest) relate to the earlier decision to use ghcr.io over Docker Hub?
qa.answer: ghcr.io was chosen for the custom pod base image because only a GitHub token was available (no Docker Hub credential); that same ghcr.io build later hit a real quirk where the build produced an attestation/provenance manifest list that GHCR sometimes rejects on the final manifest write, even though all individual layers pushed fine.

evidence.quote: Yes — ghcr.io is the right call here: there's no Docker Hub credential anywhere in the secrets vault, only a GitHub token.
That's a known GHCR quirk — the build produced an attestation/provenance manifest list that GHCR sometimes rejects on the final manifest write.

qa.question: The pod ID udk4kfi83tx5st shows up again later in the project's history, in a completely different context. What was it used for the second time?
qa.answer: It was used as the known ground-truth answer for a real-pipeline retrieval-miss probe: the fact 'Pod udk4kfi83tx5st is now stopped...' was confirmed stored verbatim in the coding-domain memory database, but did not surface in the top-5 results for a question asking about it — demonstrating a retrieval/ranking miss, not a storage miss.

evidence.quote: Confirmed: that pod ID **was** stored verbatim (`T17: "Pod udk4kfi83tx5st is now stopped..."`) — it just didn't surface in the top-5 for that specific question phrasing. Same "stored but not retrieved" pattern LoCoMo found.

qa.question: What were the two structural root causes found for the LoCoMo quality issues investigated around 2026-07-23, and which of the two is the sourceTimestamp fix?
qa.answer: Root cause #1: storage decisions are made on a single turn with zero surrounding context (no amount of adapter retraining can fix this, since the adapter is never shown the context that would make an ambiguous fact recognizable). Root cause #2 IS the sourceTimestamp issue itself: a stored memory's real sourceTimestamp was never surfaced to answer synthesis, only the narrower, derived resolvedTime — even though most 'when did X happen' questions are answered by when the message was sent, not a relative-date phrase in the text.

evidence.quote: Root cause #1 (the big one): storage decisions are made on a single turn with zero surrounding context. ... Root cause #2 (cheap, high-leverage): the turn's real timestamp (`sourceTimestamp`) is never surfaced to answer synthesis — only the narrower, derived `resolvedTime`.

qa.question: In the same-day root-cause investigation, what specific examples of turns were cited as being correctly judged 'nothing to store' in isolation but answerable when combined with the preceding turn?
qa.answer: "It's Shia Labeouf!", "Yay! My online clothes store is open!", and "Yeah! Let's make some awesome memories tomorrow at the grand opening!"

evidence.quote: Look at the "never stored" examples — turns like *"It's Shia Labeouf!"*, *"Yay! My online clothes store is open!"*, *"Yeah! Let's make some awesome memories tomorrow at the grand opening!"* get correctly judged as "nothing to store" **in isolation**.
